TASK-MCP-009 CLI REDESIGN 2

Folder Path: .claude/handoff/chain-design/2025-09-13-103229-TASK-MCP-009

*DESIGN CHAIN USING v1.3 RISK-ADAPTIVE APPROACH*
Emphasize robust error handling and uncertainty management.

Task Context:
- CLI needs facelift to meet Redesign Spec from CLI-design.md
- Analysis and execution agents should use MCP to see current state visually before further work
- Task is about visual aspect and visual interaction, not backend functionality
- Validation needed via ValidationSystem and agent-planned MCP testing
- Initial Architectural Rework Analysis needed - inconsistency in page layouts
- CLI content should determine exact layout per CLI-design rules
- Skin definition should display correctly/consistently via CLI's skin display method
- No hardcoded pages/routing - if can't work for default skin, won't work for dynamic skins
- Task complete when every item in Redesign Spec can be checked off
- ValidationSystem itself may need fixing as part of this chain
- Work should be spread *wide* - multiple analysis/validation agents, one execution agent per file/component
- Use existing patterns for implementation

risk_and_adaptation.uncertainty_handling: Probabilistic planning with confidence intervals for all duration estimates, continuous risk recalculation every 2 minutes, automated threshold-based fallback activation, and graceful degradation with acceptable outcome definitions at multiple quality levels

probabilistic_modeling.outcome_probability_distributions: Duration estimates use Beta-PERT distributions (Optimistic: 16.3min, Most Likely: 24.7min, Pessimistic: 39.2min) with 90% confidence interval [18.1, 31.8] minutes
probabilistic_modeling.uncertainty_quantification: Visual design uncertainty: ±35%, ValidationSystem status: ±25%, MCP tool reliability: ±20%, Agent coordination: ±15%. Combined uncertainty managed through defensive resource allocation and continuous monitoring
probabilistic_modeling.adaptive_architecture_details: Three-layer fallback system with real-time adaptation triggers at 2, 5, 8, 12, and 15 minute checkpoints. Each layer increases success probability while adjusting performance expectations
